summary: Asked about an Instagram post someone shared with a long caption, Nora opens the post instead of answering from the caption alone.
details: She used to see a shared post's whole caption in the chat and treat it as the whole post. With a long caption, she said there were no pictures, only text, and there were pictures. Now, for a share with a link, she sees only the opening of the caption, ending in '…', and opens the post when someone asks what is in it.
The opening is at least a real sentence's worth of words, so it does not stop at 'Mr.' or a line of emoji or hashtags, and it is never longer than 160 characters.
The full caption is still there when she opens the post. A share without a link keeps its whole caption, because there is nothing for her to open.
When she asks for a post by its link under the wrong name, the read works now instead of failing without a word.
When she tries to read an Instagram post, reel, story or profile page as an ordinary web page, she is told to open it as an Instagram post instead. It no longer goes out as a web page fetch.
limitations: What she remembers about a shared post from the chat is the opening of its caption. The rest reaches her memory only if somebody asks about the post.
Measured on replays of one recorded conversation: she opened the post 9 times in 12, not every time.
